=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:338-545 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: Mixed quoting like `e"v"al` evades the blacklist because the masking/tokenization logic splits a shell word that Bash still treats as `eval`.
  WHY: Multiple reviewers observed that quoted characters are turned into spaces before tokenization, so the validator sees harmless fragments while Bash removes the quotes and executes the banned builtin.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:394-502 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: Backslash-prefixed command names bypass the blocked-command blacklist.
  WHY: Reviewers confirmed that the masking and basename checks never normalize a leading backslash, so inputs like `\bash` and `\eval` can pass validation and still execute.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:470-525 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The `command` and `builtin` shell builtins are not treated as shell-reentry vectors.
  WHY: The validator recurses for `env` and `exec` but not for `command` or `builtin`, so payloads like `command bash -c ...` and `builtin eval ...` are accepted.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:479-513 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `exec -a` makes the shell-reentry check inspect the wrong token.
  WHY: `first_exec_command_arg` returns the `-a` value instead of the real command, so `exec -a myname bash -c ...` can bypass the check.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:338-361 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Unquoted `$(...)` command substitution is not detected outside double quotes.
  WHY: The scanner only flags `$(` inside double quotes, so inputs like `echo $(whoami)` or `$(bash -c ...)` are left intact for runtime expansion.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:443-495 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: `env` options that consume arguments can make the validator inspect the option value instead of the real command.
  WHY: The helper skips every dash-prefixed token without special-casing options like `-C`, so `/tmp` or `dir` is checked where `bash` should be.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:498-545 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: A redirection token at the end of a command is silently accepted even when its target is missing.
  WHY: The validator advances past the redirection token without verifying a following operand, so malformed input like `echo >` passes.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:544-693 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The validator skips all heredoc bodies without preserving whether the delimiter was quoted, so unquoted heredocs can still expand at runtime.
  WHY: Quoted and unquoted delimiters are collapsed to the same metadata, and the body skip lets `<<EOF` with `$(...)` or backticks evade validation.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:650-675 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Trailing whitespace on a heredoc terminator line causes a false unterminated-heredoc rejection.
  WHY: The matcher uses exact equality against the delimiter instead of trimming the candidate line.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:691-729 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: Heredoc untermination errors get wrapped with a duplicated `rejected:` prefix.
  WHY: The inner failure message already includes `rejected:`, and the outer handler prepends the same label again.
- tests/test_review_synthesise_smoke.py:393-452 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The regression test only covers two unsafe constructs and misses several bypass vectors.
  WHY: The cases list does not exercise backslash-prefixed commands, `command`/`builtin`, mixed quoting variants, or heredoc/body edge cases, so validator regressions can slip through.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:954-959 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The extractor stderr variable names are easy to confuse and swap.
  WHY: Both names encode stderr redirection plus the source stream, so the distinction between stdout- and stderr-derived extraction runs is easy to miss.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:394-502 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Backslash-prefixed command names bypass the blacklist.
  WHY: The masking function preserves the backslash and `command_basename()` does not normalize it away, so `\bash`/`\eval` can pass validation and still execute.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:489-513 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `command` and `builtin` shell builtins are not treated as shell-reentry vectors. (2 related items)
  WHY: `validate_command` recurses for `env` and `exec`, but not for `command` or `builtin`, so `command bash -c ...` and `builtin eval ...` can bypass the blacklist.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:479-486 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `exec -a` argv[0] handling inspects the wrong token.
  WHY: `first_exec_command_arg` returns the `-a` value instead of the real command, so `exec -a myname bash -c ...` can bypass shell-reentry detection.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:379-393 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Mixed quoting like `e"v"al` evades the blacklist.
  WHY: The double-quote masking turns quoted characters into spaces, splitting what Bash treats as one word into non-banned tokens.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:562-662 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Heredoc delimiter parsing discards quoting state, so heredoc bodies are skipped even when they are unquoted and expandable.
  WHY: `parse_heredoc_openers` collapses quoted and unquoted delimiters to the same metadata, so `validate_shell_content` cannot tell when `$(...)` inside a heredoc would execute.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:665-729 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Heredoc untermination diagnostics end up with a duplicated `rejected:` prefix.
  WHY: The inner failure message already says `rejected:`, and the outer exception wrapper prefixes `rejected:` again.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:670-675 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: Trailing whitespace on a heredoc delimiter line causes a false rejection.
  WHY: The delimiter matcher uses exact string equality instead of trimming the candidate line, so `PY ` does not match `PY`.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:530-533 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A redirection token at the end of the token stream is silently accepted.
  WHY: `index += 2` skips past a missing redirection target without flagging malformed shell syntax.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:954-955 | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The extraction stderr variable names are confusing and easy to swap.
  WHY: The names encode both the source stream and the captured stderr, making them maintenance hazards.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:439-513 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Backslash-escaped command names bypass the blacklist.
  WHY: `\bash` remains `\bash` through masking and basename extraction, so it does not match the banned command list.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:489-513 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `command` shell builtin is not blocked.
  WHY: `validate_command` checks `env` and `exec` recursion but not `command`, so `command bash -c '...'` passes validation.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:516-545 | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Mixed quoting such as `e"v"al` tokenizes into non-banned fragments.
  WHY: The validator does not normalize tokens that Bash later concatenates into `eval`.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:544-693 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Quoted and unquoted heredocs are not distinguished, so unquoted heredoc bodies are skipped without validation.
  WHY: The parser drops delimiter-quoting state, but unquoted heredocs can expand `$(...)`, backticks, and variables at runtime.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:691-729 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Heredoc untermination errors get wrapped with a duplicate `rejected:` prefix.
  WHY: The inner and outer failure paths both prepend `rejected:`, producing redundant diagnostics.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:667-671 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Heredoc delimiter matching uses exact equality without trimming trailing whitespace.
  WHY: A line like `PY ` will not match delimiter `PY`, so valid input is rejected as unterminated.
- scripts/review_synthesise_smoke.sh:483-489 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `env` options that take arguments can cause the helper to inspect the option value instead of the real command.
  WHY: The helper skips every dash-prefixed token unconditionally, so `env -C /path bash` can be misread.
